svg.title: Who still controls the funds?
svg.desc: Keeping old rules can leave vulnerable funds exposed under the stated quantum-attack condition. Restricting those rules can lock out owners who still control funds. Inactivity alone does not establish lost keys.

g.font-family: Arial, PingFang SC, Noto Sans CJK SC, sans-serif
g.text: BITCOIN / POST-QUANTUM MIGRATION
Who still controls the funds?
A wallet can stay untouched for years while its owner still has the keys.
Keep the old spending rules
Vulnerable funds may remain open to theft
if attackers acquire the relevant quantum
capability.
Exposure depends on the funds and attack
conditions.
Restrict the old spending rules
Making funds unspendable may also lock
out owners who still control them.
r8 opposes forced disposal.
Inactivity does not establish lost keys
Early mining history, present control and migration status describe different things.
Some holders can sign but have not acted. Others lack the credentials needed for an
ordinary migration.
Most funds migrated: what remains?
The treatment of residual funds still needs a decision.
The May 2025 Milton/Shikhelman report separately examines this ownership dilemma.
@balance0014
Source agreement on an ownership dilemma does not imply agreement on every forecast or proposed
mechanism.
Framework: @r8raq · Explanation: Balance Zhao
Sources: R4, P2 · See sources.md for scope
